problem_type: Stopping a running paid batch from the card did nothing: the card's close button went through the same busy gate as the actions it was meant to interrupt, and the host refused it on a quote the batch itself had just replaced
symptom: Real app, final head of #947, fixture vendor (2026-10-02): press Generate remaining 6, wait until the host has approved the first one, press × on the card. Nothing happens; all six are sent and the card closes as 'every shot decided', not as 'the user closed it'. Repeated in Chinese and English, with × tried every 2 seconds while 6, 6, 3 and 1 shots were still undecided. Meanwhile the card kept showing the next undecided shot with Remove and Generate this one, as if it were waiting for a click, while the host approved it on its own. Second walk on the fixed head (2026-10-02 afternoon): on a 3-shot card, press Generate this one and × right after it; the × reached the host after the approval had replaced the quote, was refused as generation_quote_changed, and the card stayed open with the other two shots.
direct_cause: src/workbench/ai/v4/useAgentPanelSpendConfirm.ts: discard (the ×) ran through act(), which returns at once while busy is true, and Generate remaining keeps busy true for the whole batch (about 3 seconds per shot). electron/capabilityCore/appIntegrationSpendConfirm.ts discardPendingSpend only accepted the card's current quoteId, while every decision on the card replaces it (each approved shot of Generate remaining, a single Generate this one, Remove), so a × sent with the quote the person saw was refused as generation_quote_changed whenever it arrived after that action.
class_root: The renderer had one gate for every card action and treated the stop like another spend action; the host-level tests for 'stop in the middle' called the host's withdraw directly, so they stayed green while the only path a person can take (the card's ×) never reached it. The same gate swallowed Remove and Generate this one while a single confirm was in flight, without any visible sign.
affected_population: Everyone who presses Generate remaining N and wants to stop it: all N are generated and paid
Everyone who presses Remove / Generate this one / × while a single confirm is still on its way (1-3 seconds): the press is swallowed without any sign
entry_points: The card's ×: slot-dismiss -> useAgentPanelSpendConfirm.discard -> productionRunApi.discardSpend -> IPC discard-spend -> appIntegrationSpendConfirm.discardPendingSpend

Generate remaining N: batch -> useAgentPanelSpendConfirm.confirmRemaining -> persistShown (one revise per page) -> IPC confirm-spend-remaining -> appIntegrationSpendConfirm.confirmRemainingShots (one confirmOneShot per shot)
Typing while the card is open and stopping the turn close the presentation through the lane (withdrawPresentation), not through the card's gate
internal_only_reason: How a paid card is answered, withdrawn and stopped in the middle is Nomi's own spend-authority flow; no external protocol defines it.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Where a running batch stops, and how many shots were approved before it stopped, is decided only by the host: confirmRemainingShots checks between shots whether the card is still open and returns batchStopped, and discardPendingSpend accepts any quote a decision on the card replaced in the open presentation (noteReplacing in confirmOneShot and removePendingSpendShot; not for edits, C09). The renderer only sends the × at once and draws what the host projects. The harness test goes through the renderer's real busy gate, which the host-level tests bypassed.

invariants: The card's × reaches the host whenever it is pressed; nothing the card is doing at that moment can swallow it.
A stopped Generate remaining sends exactly the shots approved before the stop, and the card says how many were sent and how many were not.
While a batch is running the card does not offer per-shot actions; while a single action is on its way the other actions are visibly disabled.

door_reduction.why_not: The stop still has one owner (confirmRemainingShots decides where a running batch stops; discardPendingSpend is the × it listens for). Every added door is a reader of that one result: the quotes of a running batch (read only by discardPendingSpend), the batchStopped field on the action result (declared once, read by the card hook), and the card's progress / disabled state (drawn from the host projection by projectSpendCard and the card component). The IPC handler stays the single route from the renderer.

generality_proof: Nothing depends on the model, vendor, shot kind or batch size: the host stops between any two shots of any batch, the renderer sends the × for any card, and the progress and the summary read the host's projection and the click-time stack (image or video wording through the same orderWording rule as the title).

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Approves the stack one shot at a time, checks between shots whether the card was closed, and reports how many were approved before a stop.

Withdraws the offer; accepts any quote that a decision on the card (Generate this one, Remove, each shot of Generate remaining) replaced in the presentation that is still open. A quote replaced by an edit is not accepted (C09: a delayed close cannot dismiss a newer displayed quote), and an Agent re-bid is a new presentation, so an old card's × is still refused.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: No longer goes through act(): during a batch it marks the stop (the persist loop stops before the next page; after hand-over it sends the × at once); during a single confirm it is sent at once. spend-panel-write-ownership.test.mjs covers both through the real gate.
Stay behind the gate on purpose (the shot they would act on is already being confirmed), but are now visibly disabled (actionsDisabled), and during a batch they are not drawn at all.

same_class_entry_points.entry_point: typing while the card is open / stopping the turn
same_class_entry_points.evidence: These close the presentation through withdrawPresentation in the lane, not through the card's gate; the running batch sees the card closed at its next check and reports batchStopped the same way.

recurrence.reason: The host-level test of 'stop in the middle' (agentPanelSpendRemaining.e2e) bypassed the renderer, so the green test and the broken user path coexisted; the same shape (a stop routed through the gate of the thing it stops) can come back with any new long-running card action.
same_class_scan: rg "act\(async" src/workbench/ai/v4/useAgentPanelSpendConfirm.ts -> confirm, confirmRemaining, remove, and the non-busy × path; the × no longer depends on busy

prevention.invariant: A running batch stops at the host between shots when the card is closed, and reports how many shots were approved before the stop; the card's × is never queued behind the card's other actions.
prevention.failure_mode: If the × arrives after the last shot was approved, nothing is left to stop: the card has already closed with every shot decided, and the result says so.
prevention.strategy: Send the × from the renderer without the busy gate; let the host accept the quotes the card's decisions replaced in the open presentation and return batchStopped; show progress instead of per-shot actions while the batch runs.

legacy_paths.rationale: Deleted in place: the × going through act() and being dropped while busy; the host's exact-quote-only check for a × that arrives after a decision on the card replaced the quote (first narrowed to a running batch, runningBatches; that narrowing is removed too).

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency handles the card's actions.

residual_risks: While the host approves a shot, the main process blocks the UI thread for about 2 seconds at a time (pre-existing: project-folder containment checks on every run read, and the module registry rebuilt from the catalog on every read). A × pressed then reaches the host one or two shots later; in the fixture walk the stop landed after 4 and 5 of 6. Reported to the coordinator as its own lane.

With the network down, Generate remaining still approves every shot locally and each then fails to send; nothing is charged, but each has to be retried (known limitation for 0.23; 0.24 stops the batch on the first send that fails for network reasons).
